question: Why do we use an intersectoral team approach in health care?

options.A: To combine different sectors to address the root causes of poor health
options.B: To train doctors to perform duties traditionally handled by agricultural workers
options.C: To increase the cost of running primary health care centers
options.D: To merge all community clinics into a single administrative unit

explanation: Great job! Health isn't just about medicine—it depends on social, economic, and environmental factors. Bringing different fields together helps us tackle these big issues at their core. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h1)

question: Why is just treating medical symptoms often not enough for a community?

options.A: Patients refuse to visit primary health care clinics unless accompanied by local leaders
options.B: Environmental and social root causes like poor water or housing will keep causing new illnesses
options.C: Doctors usually prescribe the wrong medications for community outbreaks
options.D: Medical treatments are too expensive for the government to maintain long-term

explanation: Spot on! If we treat a patient in the clinic but send them back to drink contaminated water, they'll just fall sick again. We have to fix the environment too! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h1)

question: Which principle of intersectoral collaboration focuses on putting the most vulnerable people first?
explanation: You've got it! Equity means fairness—making sure resources and care reach the people who need them the most, rather than just splitting everything equally. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h2)

question: Why is it so important for the local community to actively take part in health programs?

options.A: It prevents nurses from having to visit households in remote villages
options.B: It eliminates the need for any financial support from the federal ministry
options.C: It legally binds the local government to fund the health center indefinitely
options.D: It ensures that projects address real local needs and encourages people to maintain them

explanation: Exactly! When community members help plan a project, they feel a sense of ownership and are much more likely to keep it running successfully. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h2)

question: Which government sector is mainly responsible for teaching health habits and running school hygiene programs?
explanation: Correct! Schools are our best platform for teaching children and youth healthy habits that last a lifetime. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h3)

question: As a community health nurse, you notice many toddlers are malnourished in a farming village. Which non-medical sector should you involve first?
explanation: Well done! Agriculture deals with food production and farming, making them our key partner in beating chronic malnutrition at its root. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h3)

question: What is one of the main roles of a community health nurse in an intersectoral team?

options.A: Acting as a bridge connecting community members with other developmental sectors
options.B: Managing hospital budgets for the entire state health ministry
options.C: Taking over the administrative duties of local government chairpersons
options.D: Constructing boreholes and building roads without outside assistance

explanation: Right! Nurses serve as the vital link between health needs and sectors like water, education, and agriculture to solve problems together. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h4)

question: If you notice that a broken borehole is causing waterborne illnesses, what role are you mainly playing?
explanation: Spot on! Spotting a health issue and tracing it back to environmental problems is what a needs assessment is all about. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h4)

question: Why do intersectoral teams sometimes struggle to communicate with each other?

options.A: Nurses refuse to share office space with workers from other government departments
options.B: Government policies legally forbid workers from different ministries from talking
options.C: Different professional sectors use unique terminology and focus on different priorities
options.D: Community leaders only communicate through written memos in foreign languages

explanation: Exactly! Every profession has its own special terms. If we don't use simple, shared language, misunderstandings happen easily. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h5)

question: What is a great way to keep a multisectoral team accountable and working well together?

options.A: Holding meetings only once every five years to review old records
options.B: Leaving each sector to work completely independently without reporting back
options.C: Establishing joint monitoring committees with representatives from all involved sectors
options.D: Allowing the health ministry to make all decisions without consulting others

explanation: Correct! Joint committees help everyone stay on the same page, track shared goals, and solve problems as a team. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to teamwork across sectors in Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive funding and immediate budget releases for all health programs
options.B: Sectoral sidelining and agencies operating in isolation
options.C: Bureaucratic red tape between different government tiers
options.D: Frequent changes in local political leadership

explanation: You got it! Chronic underfunding and delayed budgets are huge hurdles—we definitely don't have the problem of 'too much money'! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h6)

question: What happens when government ministries work completely in isolation on health issues?

options.A: Community members take over all administrative responsibilities
options.B: Health workers receive higher salaries from the finance department
options.C: Opportunities to address the root causes of disease through shared resources are lost
options.D: The need for primary health care centers is completely eliminated

explanation: Spot on! When agencies refuse to cooperate, we miss out on team solutions for things like clean water, sanitation, and education. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h6)

question: What is the best sign that an intersectoral health program is truly sustainable?

options.A: The federal government takes over all local day-to-day management
options.B: The community takes ownership and maintains the project after external support ends
options.C: Foreign donors continue funding the program for at least twenty years
options.D: The local clinic stops seeing patients and focuses only on administrative reports

explanation: Well done! True sustainability means the community is strong enough to keep things running locally all by themselves. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h7)

question: Who should be involved when checking if an intersectoral health program was successful?

options.B: All participating sectors and community representatives
options.D: Only the federal minister of health

explanation: Correct! Because many groups built the project together, everyone involved—including the community—needs a voice in evaluating how it went. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T25#GNS225_U2_T25_h7)
